title: Polymorphism and Interfaces
learningObjectives: Explain the main paradigm or design technique.
Identify how behavior and responsibilities are organized.
Trace the provided examples and predict results.
Describe an advantage and a trade-off.
Apply the technique to a small design scenario.

understand.concept: Polymorphism allows code to work with different types through a shared operation or contract while each type can provide its own behavior. Interfaces describe a set of operations a type promises to provide in languages with explicit interfaces. Other languages may use protocols, structural typing, or duck typing.
understand.whyItMatters: Polymorphism helps callers depend on stable abstractions rather than concrete types, supporting extensibility and substitution. Poorly designed contracts or inconsistent implementations can make behavior surprising.
understand.analogy: Different devices can respond to the same control command in their own way; software contracts must define expected behavior.
understand.analogyLimit: The analogy is simplified; language features, contracts, and runtime behavior vary.

explain.narrative: Trace each example and identify the contract or style it demonstrates. Consider how a caller depends on the behavior, what could change, and where the approach might become rigid or unclear. Paradigms are design tools; avoid forcing a style when a simpler structure is more readable.

examples.title: Same contract, different result
examples.explanation: The caller invokes a shared operation on different object types.

examples.title: Interface-like contract
examples.code:
const speakers=[{play(){return 'beep';}},{play(){return 'ring';}}];
for(const s of speakers) console.log(s.play());
examples.explanation: Both values provide the operation expected by the caller; JavaScript does not require a declared interface here.

examples.title: Duck typing
examples.explanation: The function depends on the object's available behavior rather than a declared type.

examples.title: Substitution
examples.explanation: Different objects can be used where the same required property is available, though explicit contracts may be stronger.

examples.title: Contract mismatch
examples.explanation: An object missing the expected contract produces an unexpected result; contracts should be checked or typed.

commonMistakes: Using inheritance only to share code without a meaningful relationship.
Assuming an interface guarantees correct behavior by itself.
Treating imperative and declarative approaches as mutually exclusive.

questions.prompt: What is the common difference between inheritance and composition?
options: Inheritance derives from another type; composition combines parts or capabilities
questions.answer: Inheritance derives from another type; composition combines parts or capabilities
questions.explanation: Inheritance specializes a parent type; composition assembles separate components.
